text: What does it mean that a method's parameters are its interface and its locals are not?
choices: Locals are optimised away by the JIT, so they have no runtime existence to expose.
Parameters are type-checked at the call site while locals are checked only within the body.
Parameters are stored on the heap and locals on the stack, so only parameters persist.
Callers can see and must supply the parameters; the locals are invisible, so renaming or removing them cannot break anyone.
explanation: This is the smallest instance of the boundary idea that runs through the book. The parameter list is a commitment — changing it is a breaking change for every caller — and everything inside is free to change. Chapter 12 supplies the mechanism that makes the second half true: each call gets its own frame, so a method's locals cannot be reached or disturbed by anything it calls.
